description:
**Decision:** Adopt Blueprinter as the standard JSON serialization layer, replacing model-level `as_json` overrides. This follows the GitLab/Discourse pattern of separating serialization from domain models.

**Why Blueprinter:**
- Built-in views system (`:index`, `:show`, `:editor`) — different shapes per context
- `blueprinter-activerecord` companion gem for automatic N+1 prevention
- Already adopted in v3.x for some endpoints — forward-compatible
- 2x faster than `to_json` with Oj backend
- Backed by Procore (not a solo maintainer)
- Incremental adoption — coexists with existing `as_json` during migration

**Research basis:**
- GitLab uses grape-entity with `with_api_entity_associations` scopes
- Discourse uses custom PORO serializers with context subclasses
- Mastodon uses AMS (legacy, wouldn't choose today)
- Thoughtbot explicitly calls `as_json` overrides an anti-pattern
- Community consensus (2025-2026): Blueprinter or Alba, never AMS

**Current state:**
- Gems installed: blueprinter 1.2.1, blueprinter-activerecord 1.3.0, oj 3.16.16
- Initializer created: config/initializers/blueprinter.rb
- Blueprint directory created: app/blueprints/
- No blueprints written yet

**Models needing blueprints (priority order):**
1. Rule/BaseRule — worst N+1 offender, foundation for everything
2. Component — most complex show page, 9 methods in to_json
3. Stig — xml blob exclusion
4. SecurityRequirementsGuide — xml blob exclusion
5. Review, Membership, User (compact), SrgRule, StigRule, Check, DisaRuleDescription

**Controllers to migrate:**
1. ComponentsController — show, find, index
2. RulesController — index, show, related_rules
3. StigsController — index, show
4. SecurityRequirementsGuidesController — index, show
5. Api::SearchController — all search methods
6. ProjectsController — index, show

description:
VulcanAudit#find_and_save_associated_rule uses bitwise `&` instead of logical `&&` in its nil check, causing NoMethodError crashes at runtime.

**Location**: `app/lib/vulcan_audit.rb:43`

**Buggy code**:
```ruby
self.audited_username = "Control #{rule&.displayed_name}" if rule.present? & rule.component.present?
```

**Why it crashes**: `&` (bitwise AND) does NOT short-circuit. When `rule` is nil, `rule.present?` returns false, but Ruby still evaluates `rule.component` which raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'component' for nil`. The leading `rule&.displayed_name` safe-navigation proves the author knew rule could be nil, but the guard itself explodes before the body runs.

**Trigger**: Any audit callback where the associated Rule record has been deleted (e.g. component deletion cascade, orphaned BaseRule audit entries).

**Why:** Silent critical production bug that will crash the audit callback chain whenever a rule is missing.
**How to apply:** Fix with short-circuit + early return. Add regression tests for nil rule path.
title: Fix VulcanAudit bitwise & causing NoMethodError on nil rule

title: Fix OIDC provider conflict: symbol/string bug, auto-link, clear UX messaging

description:
**Problem:** Heroku staging Okta login fails for ALL users with a generic "unexpected error" message. Root cause is a symbol/string comparison bug in `User.from_omniauth` — OmniAuth returns `provider` as a symbol (`:oidc`) while the DB stores a string (`"oidc"`), so `user.provider != auth.provider` is always true, incorrectly triggering `ProviderConflictError`. Error is hidden because `rescue_from StandardError` is defined AFTER the specific `ProviderConflictError` handler, so Rails checks it first and catches it.

**Scope creep:** Bug hunt expanded into a UX pass on provider linking, session auth method tracking, unlink feature, and 13 pre-existing bug-scan findings in auth/user code.

## Completed work (uncommitted, on branch fix/oidc-provider-conflict)

### Core bug fixes
- [x] `User.from_omniauth`: provider+uid lookup first, `.to_s` coercion (fixes symbol/string)
- [x] `OmniauthCallbacksController`: `rescue_from` ordering fixed (StandardError defined first)
- [x] `oauth_error` handler: removed `exception.message` from flash (prevents info leakage)
- [x] Removed unnecessary `save!` on re-auth path (prevents wasted DB writes)

### Features
- [x] `VULCAN_AUTO_LINK_USER` global setting (single "one ring" setting for all providers)
- [x] SECURITY: `email_verified` check — refuses auto-link when provider asserts `email_verified=false`
- [x] `User#just_auto_linked?` transient flag — removes duplicate email lookup in controller
- [x] Session auth method tracking (`session[:auth_method]`) — distinguishes "signed in via" from "linked to"
- [x] Profile UI: shows "Signed in via X" + "Account also linked to Y" separately
- [x] Unlink identity feature: `/users/unlink_identity` with password verification, lockout prevention, audit
- [x] Audit comments for link/unlink events (`user.audit_comment = ...`)
- [x] History component: suppresses raw "field updated" text when audit has a comment

### Gem / Ruby / infrastructure
- [x] Replaced `gitlab_omniauth-ldap` → `omniauth-ldap` 2.3.3 (drops kconv/nkf dead dependency)
- [x] Removed `nkf` gem — Ruby VM bug #21967 no longer reachable
- [x] Ruby 3.4.8 → 3.4.9
- [x] `require 'ostruct'` in login_helpers (Ruby 3.4 stdlib removal)
- [x] `parallel_sync.rake` infinite recursion fix (TEST_ENV_NUMBER guard)

### Bugs fixed during work (not originally in scope)
- [x] My Activity panel: `userHistories` filter used `h.user_id` which `VulcanAudit#format` doesn't emit — never matched, activity was silently empty. Removed redundant filter (controller already scopes by user).

### Tests added
- 62 backend auth tests (user_okta, user_ldap, critical_edge_cases, edge_cases)
- 5 session auth method tests
- 10 unlink_identity tests
- 26 UserProfile Vue tests

## Pending work (see child cards)

- 13 bug-scan findings (3 fixes applied, 10 not yet fixed) — each with own card + TDD requirement
- 2 future features (link button symmetry, lockout on bad unlink)
- 3 research cards documenting decisions

- [ ] Live tested on dev (local login + Okta login + unlink + error paths)

description:
**Location:** `app/controllers/users_controller.rb:70-72`

**Buggy code:**
```ruby
if @user.update(user_update_params)
  notification_type = @user.admin ? :assign_vulcan_admin : :remove_vulcan_admin
  send_slack_notification(notification_type, @user) if Settings.slack.enabled
```

**Problem:** Every successful user update fires a Slack notification as either "assign_vulcan_admin" or "remove_vulcan_admin" — regardless of whether the admin flag actually changed. A simple name change broadcasts "User demoted from vulcan admin" to Slack.

**Fix:** Gate on `@user.saved_change_to_admin?`.

**Status:** Fix applied in working tree. Tests NOT yet written.

**Why:** Slack spam damages trust in notifications; false "promoted/demoted" messages confuse ops team.
**How to apply:** Only notify when admin flag actually changed, not on every update. TDD required.
title: Fix Slack notification firing on every user update instead of only admin changes

description:
**Location:** `app/javascript/components/users/UsersTable.vue:162-164`

**Current code:**
```js
typeColumn: function (user) {
  return user.provider === null ? "Local User" : user.provider.toUpperCase() + " User";
}
```

**Problem:** Strict equality with `null`. Rails `as_json` emits `null` for a nil column when the field is in `select`, so existing call sites are safe. But any future caller passing a user object WITHOUT the `provider` key (new endpoint, test fixture, v-bind with partial data) will hit `undefined.toUpperCase()` → TypeError. EditUserModal.vue's `providerLabel` uses `!user.provider ?` — the idiomatic pattern.

**Fix:** Use falsy check:
```js
typeColumn: (user) => !user.provider ? "Local User" : user.provider.toUpperCase() + " User"
```

**Status:** NOT yet fixed.
title: Use falsy check in UsersTable typeColumn to handle undefined provider

description:
**Location:** `app/constants/project_member_constants.rb:9`

**Current code:**
```ruby
PROJECT_MEMBER_VIEWERS = %w[viewer reviewer author admin].freeze
PROJECT_MEMBER_AUTHORS = %w[author admin].freeze
PROJECT_MEMBER_REVIEWERS = %w[reviewer admin].freeze
PROJECT_MEMBER_ADMINS = 'admin'   # <-- singular string, plural name
```

**Problem:** Siblings are arrays. `PROJECT_MEMBER_ADMINS` is a scalar string with a plural name. Used in `user.rb`:
```ruby
project.memberships.where(user_id: id, role: PROJECT_MEMBER_ADMINS).any?
```
Works because ActiveRecord accepts a scalar. But any future caller who assumes array semantics (`PROJECT_MEMBER_ADMINS.include?(role)`) gets String#include? which is substring match, not membership check. Footgun.

**Fix:** Normalize to an array: `PROJECT_MEMBER_ADMINS = %w[admin].freeze`. Update any references that assume a scalar.

**Status:** NOT yet fixed. Consider whether in-scope for this PR or follow-up.
title: Normalize PROJECT_MEMBER_ADMINS constant to array for consistency with siblings

description:
**Location:** `app/controllers/users/registrations_controller.rb:95` (in `unlink_identity` action)

**Issue:**
```ruby
unless user.valid_password?(params[:current_password].to_s)
```

**Hidden side effect:** `User#valid_password?` is overridden in user.rb:56 to do bcrypt→PBKDF2 rehashing on successful login:
```ruby
def valid_password?(password)
  if encrypted_password.start_with?('$2a$', '$2b$')
    # ... verify with BCrypt ...
    update_columns(encrypted_password: new_hash, password_salt: new_salt) if result
  else
    super
  end
end
```

So calling `valid_password?` in `unlink_identity` has a hidden write side-effect when the user still has a legacy bcrypt password. Not a bug today — the rehash is idempotent — but:
1. Unlink would fail silently on a read-only DB replica
2. The write happens during what looks like a read/verify step
3. A future refactor might break the assumption

**Fix:** Add a code comment at the unlink call site explicitly referencing `User#valid_password?` override and its migration write. No code change needed today, but document the dependency.

**Status:** NOT yet fixed. Documentation-only card.
title: Document valid_password? hidden rehash side-effect at unlink call site

description:
**Context:** We now have an "Unlink" button in the profile for users with a linked external identity. The symmetrical opposite — a "Link with <provider>" button — does not exist. After unlinking, a user can only re-link by signing out, signing in via OIDC, and relying on `VULCAN_AUTO_LINK_USER=true` email matching.

**Proposed flow:**
1. Profile shows "Link with Okta" button when `user.provider` is nil and an OIDC provider is configured
2. Click → session flag `link_in_progress: true` is set, user redirected to `/users/auth/oidc`
3. OmniauthCallbacksController detects `session[:link_in_progress]` + existing signed-in user → attaches the returning OIDC identity to the current user (doesn't create new account)
4. Edge case: if the returning OIDC identity already belongs to another account, refuse with clear error
5. Audit the link event via `audit_comment`

**Files:**
- `app/views/devise/registrations/edit.html.haml` or UserProfile.vue — new button
- `app/controllers/users/omniauth_callbacks_controller.rb` — detect link mode
- `app/controllers/users/registrations_controller.rb` — new `initiate_link` action (sets session flag)
- `config/routes.rb` — POST `/users/initiate_link`
- `spec/requests/users/initiate_link_spec.rb` — new spec

**Why:** UX symmetry. Users who unlink should be able to re-link without admin help or env var gymnastics.
**How to apply:** After main v2.3.1 fix is merged. Not blocking release.
title: Add 'Link with <provider>' button in profile for symmetry with Unlink

description:
**Context:** Current unlink flow requires current password verification (CSRF + account ownership proof). But there's no rate limit on bad attempts — an attacker with a stolen session could brute-force the password via unlink.

**Proposed approach:** Reuse Devise's `:lockable` module infrastructure. On failed `valid_password?` in unlink_identity, call `user.failed_attempts += 1` and `user.lock_access!` when threshold reached.

**Option A (simple):** Manual increment in the unlink controller rescue path
**Option B (proper):** Wrap the password check so Devise's built-in failed_attempts tracking handles it

**Security win:** Same lockout semantics as failed login (3 attempts, 15 min unlock per `VULCAN_LOCKOUT_*` settings).

**Why:** Unlink is a privileged account operation; same lockout protection as login.
**How to apply:** After main fix merged. Wire into existing Devise lockable infrastructure — don't roll a separate counter.
title: Lockout on repeated failed password attempts during unlink

description:
**Context:** Before implementing the auto-link feature we researched how major Rails apps handle OmniAuth provider conflicts and multi-provider linking.

## Findings

### GitLab
- Lookup by provider+uid FIRST, then email fallback
- `omniauth_auto_link_user` config setting (true / false / array of provider names)
- GitLab fork of omniauth-ldap was bumped to 2.3.0 (removes kconv dead require)
- Current GitLab: `gem 'gitlab_omniauth-ldap', '~> 2.3.0'`

### Discourse
- Uses separate `omniauth_identity` table (has_many :identities)
- Lookup always by (provider, uid) — never by email for security
- Auto-link is admin-approved, not auto

### Devise wiki
- Recommends the (provider, uid) → email fallback pattern
- Does NOT address the unauthenticated-user-with-matching-local-account case

### Vulcan's pick
- Single provider+uid on User model (not identity table — avoids migration)
- Global `VULCAN_AUTO_LINK_USER` setting (one ring)
- `email_verified` claim check for OIDC safety
- Human-readable error messages, clear UX

## nkf Ruby VM bug (#21967)
- Ruby 3.4+ VM crash in forked processes when nkf.so loads
- `gitlab_omniauth-ldap` 2.2.0 has dead `require 'kconv'` → loads nkf
- Fix: swap to `omniauth-ldap` 2.3.3 (original, no kconv), OR bump gitlab fork to 2.3.0
- We picked `omniauth-ldap` 2.3.3 because it's more actively maintained and has better thread-safety (option :mapping vs @@config)

**Links:**
- https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/21967
- https://github.com/omniauth/omniauth-ldap
- GitLab docs on omniauth_auto_link_user

**Why:** Document the why behind the design decisions for future maintainers.
title: Research: OmniAuth provider lookup patterns, auto-link, nkf VM bug

description:
**Context:** Extended debugging session trying to get local dev PostgreSQL working with OrbStack on a MITRE laptop with GlobalProtect VPN. Documents findings for future developers hitting the same wall.

## Findings

### OrbStack is closed-source
- Cannot inspect or patch the port forwarding proxy or DNS service
- https://github.com/orbstack/orbstack is issue tracker only, not source
- Only free for personal use, paid for commercial

### DNS cache bug (#2267 — open, no fix)
- When a container restarts, OrbStack's mDNS cache holds the OLD container IP
- `.orb.local` hostnames resolve to stale IPs even after container restart
- Workaround: assign static IPs in docker-compose (conflicts with multi-project dev)
- Enterprise users reported this since March 2026 — still open

### macOS 15 Local Network permission (#1452, #1620)
- Terminal apps need "Allow Local Network" in System Settings → Privacy & Security
- Without this, even correct OrbStack DNS fails with "no route to host"
- Common symptom: `nslookup` works but actual connection fails

### GlobalProtect VPN conflict
- GP dynamically adds routes for any 192.168.x.x subnet it sees traffic for
- OrbStack uses 192.168.x.x by default — GP captures and routes to VPN gateway
- Results in traffic to container IP going to MITRE corporate network instead of local bridge
- `netstat -rn | grep 192.168.167` shows the hijacked route via utun0

### Fix applied
- Configure OrbStack to use `198.19.x.x` subnet (not 192.168.x.x)
- OrbStack Settings → Docker → Engine:
  ```json
  {
    "tlscert": "~/.aws/mitre-ca-bundle.pem",
    "bip": "198.19.192.1/23",
    "default-address-pools": [
      {"base": "198.19.192.0/19", "size": 23},
      {"base": "198.19.224.0/20", "size": 23}
    ]
  }
  ```
- GlobalProtect does NOT claim 198.19.x.x (reserved for benchmarks RFC 2544)
- But GP will still claim any subnet OrbStack uses after restart → need to kill DNS cache

### Supplementary fix for scram-sha-256
- OrbStack's port forward proxy mangles PostgreSQL SCRAM-SHA-256 challenge-response
- Set `POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD: trust` in docker-compose.dev.yml
- Mastodon, GitLab do the same for dev/CI
- Production uses docker-compose.yml which does NOT set trust
- Documented with link to issue #2267 inline in the compose file

**Why:** Save the next developer 4 hours of debugging when they hit this.
**How to apply:** Reference this card when onboarding v2.x devs on MITRE-issued laptops.
title: Research: OrbStack + GlobalProtect VPN routing conflicts (MITRE dev env)

description:
**Context:** Original release workflow (git-cliff + tag-triggered) was removed by will (commit 604d808) because GITHUB_TOKEN couldn't push CHANGELOG.md to branch-protected master. We researched the proper industry-standard fix.

## Findings

### tj-actions supply chain attack (March 2025)
- CVE-2025-30066: compromised `tj-actions/changed-files` impacted ~23,000 repos including Coinbase (70K customers)
- Attacker retroactively modified version tags to point to malicious commits
- Tags (`@v1`, `@v2`) are MUTABLE; SHAs are not
- OpenSSF guidance post-attack: pin ALL actions to full commit SHAs

### GitHub App token pattern (industry standard)
- GitLab, Semantic Release, and others use this approach
- Create a GitHub App scoped to the repo with `contents: write`
- Add app to branch protection "Allow specified actors to bypass required pull requests"
- Store `app-id` and `private-key` as secrets
- Use `actions/create-github-app-token@<SHA>` in workflow to mint a short-lived token
- App tokens are NOT tied to a human (PATs are) and are scoped to the specific repo

### Why this is better than PATs
- PATs require a human owner — attacker who compromises the human gets everything
- App tokens are scoped, short-lived, revocable
- GitHub auto-expires app tokens after 1 hour

### What NOT to do
- Never use `pull_request_target` trigger — runs with write permissions on fork PR code
- Never skip hooks (`--no-verify`) in CI
- Never use `@main` or `@master` refs for third-party actions

**Already tracked as:** vulcan-v3.x-8ij (separate card for implementing this)

**Why:** Document the security reasoning behind the planned release workflow restoration.
**How to apply:** Reference when implementing vulcan-v3.x-8ij.
title: Research: GitHub Actions supply chain hardening post tj-actions attack

description:
**Location:** `app/controllers/users_controller.rb:250` (in `send_password_reset` action)

**Buggy code:**
```ruby
raw, hashed = Devise.token_generator.generate(User, :reset_password_token)
user.update!(reset_password_token: hashed, reset_password_sent_at: Time.current)
```

**Problem:** `update!` runs full ActiveRecord validations. If the target user record has any pre-existing validation failure (e.g. name exceeds current `Settings.input_limits.user_name`, or an old email that now fails a stricter format validator), the admin's attempt to generate a reset link raises `ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid` — blocking an unrelated admin recovery flow. Devise's own `send_reset_password_instructions` uses `save(validate: false)` internally for exactly this reason.

**Fix:** Use `update_columns` (skips validations AND callbacks; token writes carry no business logic).

**Status:** NOT yet fixed.
title: Use update_columns in send_password_reset to avoid validation blocking admin recovery

**Buggy code:**

```ruby
  render json: {
    toast: { title: 'Could not send password reset.', message: [e.message], variant: 'danger' }
  }, status: :internal_server_error
end
```

**Two problems:**
1. **Info leakage:** Echoing `e.message` to the client can leak SMTP server hostnames, auth errors, connection strings, stack hints. Compare to `omniauth_callbacks_controller.rb` which explicitly redacts.
2. **Silent server-side failure:** No `Rails.logger.error` call — the exception is swallowed server-side, making incidents undebuggable.

**Fix:** Log full exception with backtrace server-side; return a generic message to the client.

description:
**Location:** `app/controllers/users/registrations_controller.rb:117-134`

**Buggy code:**
```ruby
private
def respond_with_error(message, status) ... end
public          # <-- applies to nothing; misleading
protected
def update_resource(resource, params) ... end
```

**Problem:** Bare `public` keyword sits between `respond_with_error` (private helper I added) and `protected` (Devise overrides). It applies to NO methods — but strongly misleads readers and opens the door for a future developer to add a method in that slot, accidentally exposing what should be a private helper as a public action.

**Fix:** Put `respond_with_error` under the existing `protected` block (it's a protected helper anyway). Remove the stray `public`.

description:
**Locations:**
- `app/models/user.rb:116-117` (from_omniauth rescue)
- `app/controllers/users/omniauth_callbacks_controller.rb` (all omniauth_*_error handlers)

**Buggy pattern:**
```ruby
rescue StandardError => e
  Rails.logger.error "Failed to create/update user from OmniAuth: #{e.message}"
  Rails.logger.debug e.backtrace.join("\n") if Rails.env.development?
  raise
end
```

**Problem:** Production incidents lose the backtrace. Production operators who need to debug an OIDC failure CAN NOT get the stack trace even if they crank log level to debug — the line is gated on `Rails.env.development?`.

**Fix:** Drop the `if Rails.env.development?` gate. `Rails.logger.debug` is already conditionally emitted based on the current log level, so adding the backtrace to debug output is safe — ops can enable debug logging in production when investigating incidents.

**Status:** NOT yet fixed.
title: Log OmniAuth exception backtraces in all environments, not just development

description:
**Location:** `app/models/user.rb:166`

**Current code:**
```ruby
if auth.info.respond_to?(:email_verified) && auth.info.email_verified == false
```

**Problem:** The comment above explicitly says "If the claim is absent, we trust the admin's decision. If explicitly false, refuse." Current code correctly lets `nil` pass (since `nil == false` is `false`). But providers that encode the field as string `"false"` (misconfigured OIDC attribute mappings, some SAML-to-OIDC bridges) would be treated as verified, bypassing the security check.

**Fix:** Use `ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(...)` — it returns `nil` for absent/nil, `true` for true/"true"/1, `false` for false/"false"/0.

```ruby
email_verified_claim = auth.info.respond_to?(:email_verified) ? auth.info.email_verified : nil
if ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(email_verified_claim) == false
  # refuse
end
```

**Status:** NOT yet fixed.
title: Harden email_verified OIDC claim check against string 'false' from misconfigured providers

description:
**Problem:** Production Heroku dynos crash (R14/R15 memory, H12 timeout) on multiple endpoints due to loading multi-MB xml blobs and N+1 query patterns. The `/stigs` crash (fixed in #713) was the first symptom; code review found the same patterns across search, show pages, and rule serialization.

5. Unbounded queries without `.limit()` on audit tables
6. Ruby-level filtering instead of SQL (available_members, available_components)

**Target release:** v2.3.3 (performance hardening)

**Work order:** Cards are dependency-chained by stability impact — fix the deepest root cause first (Rule#as_json N+1) since it affects the most endpoints, then work outward.

description:
**Location:** `app/models/rule.rb:171`

**Buggy code:**
```ruby
srg_info: { version: SecurityRequirementsGuide.find_by(id: srg_rule&.security_requirements_guide_id)&.version }
```

**Problem:** Every call to `Rule#as_json` fires a separate `SecurityRequirementsGuide.find_by()` query. For a component with 200 rules, this is 200+ queries, EACH loading the full SRG record INCLUDING the multi-MB `xml` column. All 200 queries return the SAME SRG (all rules in a component share one SRG).

**Endpoints affected:** Component show, rules index, rules show, component find, related_rules, any endpoint that serializes rules.

**Fix:** All rules in a component share the same SRG via `component.based_on`. Replace the per-rule lookup with `component.based_on&.version`. If the rule doesn't have a component context, fall back to `srg_rule&.security_requirements_guide&.version` (requires eager_load).

**Why first:** This is the deepest root cause — fixing it reduces query count by 200+ per page AND eliminates 200 multi-MB xml loads per page. Every other fix that involves rendering rules benefits from this.
title: C3: Fix Rule#as_json N+1 SecurityRequirementsGuide.find_by per rule

**Problem:** 9 separate `rules.where(status: ...).size` queries. Each goes through `has_many :rules, through: :components` join. Called on every project show page.

**Fix:** Single query: `counts = rules.group(:status).count` for status counts, plus `rules.where(locked: false).where(review_requestor_id: nil).count` etc. Reduces 9 queries to 2-3.

**Depends on:** Nothing — standalone model fix.
notes: [2026-04-07] Still needs GROUP BY consolidation. Not addressed by Blueprinter migration.
title: H3: Consolidate Project#details from 9 COUNT queries to 1-2

description:
**Location:** `app/controllers/projects_controller.rb:24-33`

**Problem:** Per-project `current_user.access_requests.find_by(project_id:)` is N+1. 50 projects = 50 queries.

**Fix:** Batch: `ar_by_project = current_user.access_requests.where(project_id: project_ids).index_by(&:project_id)` then hash lookup.

**Depends on:** Nothing — standalone controller fix.
title: H4: Batch access_request lookup in ProjectsController#index

description:
**Location:** `app/controllers/components_controller.rb:426`

**Problem:** `render json: rules` triggers full `Rule#as_json` without eager loading associations (reviews, satisfies, satisfied_by, srg_rule). After C3 is fixed, the SRG N+1 is gone, but the association N+1 remains.

**Fix:** Add `.eager_load(:reviews, :satisfies, :satisfied_by, :srg_rule)` to the rules query, or use `as_json(skip_merge: true)` for search results that don't need full detail.

**Depends on:** C3 (Rule#as_json fix).
title: H5: Add eager_load to ComponentsController#find rule serialization
